name: F-16C Block 50 (open-source data)
description: Single-engine multirole fighter with the F110-GE-129. Values are public approximations; the model reproduces SEP ≈ 52 m/s and ≈ 5.7 g at 9 km, Mach 0.9, military power.

sources.MASS_EMPTY: open-source F-16C Block 50 estimate (as calibrated in f16_sim.py)

sources.DRAG_RISE_M1: where the model's rise has always peaked; see Peak extra CD
sources.DRAG_RISE_M2: peak 0.034 at Mach 0.975, decay 0.7, wave drag held beyond Mach 1.4: top speed at full afterburner is Mach 1.24 at 500 m, 1.37 at 3 km, 1.66 at 9 km and the Mach 1.8 cap at 12 km (published: ≈ 1.2 low, ≈ 2 at altitude). History: the rise was a half sine that fell back to zero just below Mach 1.1 and jumped to the peak there (a low-drag gap across Mach 1.0–1.1); now a quarter sine to the same peak at 0.975, so the curve below 0.975 is unchanged and top speed moved only at 500 m (from Mach 1.17). Before that, peak 0.040, decay 2.0 and zero drag above Mach 1.4: Mach 1.8 even at sea level

sources.T_MIL_SL: F110-GE-129, published ≈ 76 kN military installed ≈ 65 kN

sources.MACH_MAX: published ≈ Mach 2 at altitude; model cap 1.8
sources.K_ALT_GAM: tuned with bvr_perf.py: a 1 km altitude step overshoots 20 m and settles in 23 s at 340 m/s (0 m at 250 m/s), with a 3.1 g pull-up; was K_ALT_GAM 0.12, K_GAM_NZ 3.0: 254 m overshoot, 48 s
sources.K_GAM_NZ: tuned with bvr_perf.py: a 1 km altitude step overshoots 20 m and settles in 23 s at 340 m/s (0 m at 250 m/s), with a 3.1 g pull-up; was K_ALT_GAM 0.12, K_GAM_NZ 3.0: 254 m overshoot, 48 s
sources.K_V_THROT: tuned with bvr_perf.py speed_check: PI speed hold, steady error ≤ 0.4 m/s and overshoot ≤ 1.1 m/s for steps between 220 and 400 m/s at 3 and 9 km. Was proportional only (0.012): steady errors up to 34 m/s
